bullets.title: AVGO earnings disappoint on AI revenue guide, triggering broad semi selloff
bullets.body: Broadcom 2Q revenue beat and 3Q guide above consensus, but FY27 AI revenue ($100B+/10GW maintained) fell short of elevated buy-side expectations of $150B+, sending the stock down 14-15%. The miss exposed stretched positioning across semis: SOXX -4%, MU -5.7%, AMD -4%, SMCI -7.2%. Wolfe and JPM argue FY27 guide is intentionally conservative—AVGO projects 3GW to Anthropic and 1.3GW to OpenAI in 2H27 alone, with FY28 shaping up as the true XPU supercycle year as Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic deployments fully materialize.

bullets.title: Semi/tech selloff is momentum unwind, not risk-off—software and pharma/financials rotating bid
bullets.body: Equal-weight S&P up 70bps while cap-weighted is flat; AVGO, MU, AMD alone account for 70bps of drag on the index. 12-month losers are up 2.5%, winners down 1.5%—a substantial momentum unwind. Pharma and financials (worst YTD sectors) up 2%+ on the day; the desk characterizes this as money moving into catalysts rather than a de-risking signal.

bullets.title: Levered ETF short gamma at record levels creates tail risk in semis/tech on any catalyst
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley QDS flags levered equity ETF AUM up 50% YTD to $300bn, controlling $750bn in global equities. Semis carry record $4.75bn short gamma on a 1% move (80% from index products). HF net exposure to Japan, South Korea, Taiwan at 15-year highs; memory >10% of HF books. A macro or micro catalyst (inflation print, chip supply surprise) could trigger non-linear sell acceleration; MS recommends buying puts on Long Momentum basket or KOSPI2 put spreads.

bullets.title: AI narrative shifts from discovery to digestion—stocks now reflect fair pricing, execution matters
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side notes converge on the view that the AI trade has moved from disbelief to broad acceptance, raising the bar for further re-rating. Broadcom's strong results underwhelming, trillion-dollar capex announcements now routine, and broad sector participation (networking, optical, memory, storage, power) signal late-stage theme recognition. Short-term consolidation expected before next leg; macro headwinds (Hormuz, grid constraints, geopolitical pre-midterms) are now two-sided risk factors.

bullets.title: Nasdaq 100 futures hit session low of -1.5%; S&P futures extend losses to -0.6%
bullets.body: Multiple intraday headlines confirm NDX futures touched -1.5% and SPX futures -0.6% as session lows, driven by the AVGO-led semi selloff and broader AI positioning unwind. OPCO desk targets a mid-June pullback of 3-5% in S&P with major catalysts (CPI June 10, SpaceX inclusion June 12, FOMC June 17, OpEx June 18) acting as the likely inflection points.

bullets.title: Oil down 3%+ on Iran ceasefire/peace deal hopes; Hormuz remains key macro bottleneck
bullets.body: WTI and Brent crude fell over 3% on White House signals of an Iran ceasefire being maintained unless US troops are killed, and reports of US-Iran interim deal progress. However, Iran's FM says no tangible progress exists, and only 29 of 109 tankers have escaped the Strait of Hormuz since conflict began (80 remain trapped). Drewry container index is up 80% since conflict began. Non-AI cyclicals (retail, airlines, transports, banks) remain tied to Hormuz resolution; 22V pegs odds at just 15% by end of June.

bullets.title: May jobs data: Challenger layoffs highest since May 2020; tech sector largest cutter since Aug 2024
bullets.body: US job cuts totaled 97,006 in May, the highest for that month since 2020. Tech sector alone announced 38,242 eliminations—highest since August 2024—with AI cited as the leading driver. May Challenger announcements rose 3.4% YoY vs. prior -20.9%. Partially offset by ADP showing broad-based private hiring across all firm sizes in May.

bullets.title: ISM Services new orders surge to 57.3; April factory orders +4.8% m/m—data contradicts slowdown narrative
bullets.body: ISM Services PMI new orders component jumped to 57.3 in May vs. 53.5 prior and 54.7 twelve-month average, signaling strong forward demand. April factory orders soared +4.8% m/m (largest gain since May 2025), led by 22% surge in transportation equipment. Initial jobless claims at 225k with 4-week average of 215k—historically very low—confirming labor market resilience despite rising layoff announcements.

bullets.title: Payrolls tomorrow key: JPM forecasts 75k vs. Street 85k; May CPI relief from falling gasoline
bullets.body: JPM Morgan AM forecasts May NFP at 75k (Street: 85k), unemployment at 4.3%, AHE +0.3% MoM. US gasoline prices down 7% from recent peaks and global retail fuel prices fell 1.8% last week, pointing to June CPI relief. OPCO desk does not view tomorrow's payrolls as a major catalyst; desk eyes CPI on June 10 and FOMC June 17 as the pivotal events.

bullets.title: US productivity at strongest since late 1990s on AI tailwind; unit labor costs benign
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes nonfarm business productivity rose 2.8% y/y in Q1—strongest since the late 1990s outside cyclical recoveries—driven by AI, despite q/q revision down to 0.3% a.r. due to tariff/inflation impacts. Unit labor costs at 1.8% q/q, below business output price gains, suggesting no imminent margin squeeze from labor. However, tariffs squeezed nonlabor costs.

bullets.title: Record buybacks ($533bn Apr-May) and low put-call ratio suggest complacency despite pullback
bullets.body: US tech buybacks drove a record $533bn in April-May 2026 (vs. $487bn prior year), running at ~$1.9tr annual pace. Put-call ratio near 25-year lows with little downside options enthusiasm—comparable to mid-2020 to early 2021. S&P 500 1-year implied correlation is below dot-com lows, indicating high dispersion. Jefferies notes buybacks running +44% YoY at 1.9x 2025 average daily trading volume.

bullets.title: Data center buildout constrained by power/grid, not capital; $156B of projects stalled or cancelled
bullets.body: JPMorgan estimates 60%+ of planned 2027 US data center capacity is not yet under construction, with power/grid access—not capital—as the binding constraint. Wholesale electricity prices are up 76% YoY. Approximately $156B of data center projects have been stalled or cancelled since 2025; only 26% of Americans support more data center construction. Regulatory headwinds widening: first permanent data center ban passed in Monterey Park CA, Seattle council weighing one-year moratorium.

bullets.title: China margin debt exceeds 2015 bubble peak; JPM sees AI localization dip-buying window
bullets.body: Goldman data shows China margin trading balance now higher than the peak of the 2015 bubble, signaling elevated leverage risk in Chinese equities. Separately, JPMorgan sees a tactical buy-the-dip window in China AI localization plays: STAR-ChiNext 50 is up 43% vs. MSCI China -6.1% since April with AI intensity differentiating performance; MXCN end-2026 base case target 100 on 13%/25% YoY EPS growth.

bullets.title: Bitcoin slides to 4-month low (~$61K); $1.8B in crypto liquidations
bullets.body: Bitcoin fell to $61,311 before partially rebounding, driven by geopolitical tensions, ETF outflows, and strategy Bitcoin sales. Over $1.8 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated. Bitcoin is now down ~27% YTD and 50% from its October record high. Crypto-related stocks were pressured.

bullets.title: SCOTUS upholds FCC enforcement authority; AT&T's $57M fine reinstated
bullets.body: Supreme Court ruled 8-1 that FCC's enforcement structure does not violate the 7th Amendment, reversing the Fifth Circuit ruling in favor of AT&T and affirming the Second Circuit ruling upholding Verizon's fine. AT&T's original $57M fine from 2020 for location data violations now stands. The ruling cements FCC's ability to issue forfeiture orders without jury trials.

bullets.title: OPCO targets mid-June SPX pullback of 3-5%; gamma support at 7500, breaks at 7400
bullets.body: OPCO desk flags $11B gamma support at SPX 7500 from 0DTE put selling; gamma zone support extends to ~7400 below which risk of acceleration increases. Desk targets 3-5% SPX drawdown by mid-June equating to ~15% in momentum and ~20% in semis. Catalysts: CPI June 10, SpaceX index inclusion June 12, FOMC June 17, monthly OpEx June 18.

bullets.title: North American M&A surges to $315B in May; deal activity recovering
bullets.body: North American M&A announcements increased to $315B in May from $286B in April, with higher-end property transactions showing lift. JPMorgan's lodging REIT REITweek check shows management teams increasingly optimistic about early innings of multi-year cycle.

bullets.title: SpaceX files $75B IPO at $135/share; Oppenheimer flags disruption risk for T, VZ
bullets.body: SpaceX (SPCX) filed for an IPO of 555.56M Class A shares at $135/share targeting ~$75B in capital. Oppenheimer sees SpaceX disrupting the $1.6T communications industry, raising 2030 US broadband subscriber estimates from 10M to 15M and 2035 space revenue estimates from $500B to $800B. The analyst is negative on traditional carriers (T, VZ) and positive on spectrum, AI infrastructure, and drone adjacencies.

bullets.title: Mortgage applications fell 2.5% w/w; 30-year rate dips to 6.57%—housing data stays soft
bullets.body: MBA mortgage applications for the week ended May 29 fell 2.5% (vs. -8.5% prior), with the 30-year fixed rate declining to 6.57% from 6.65%. Workers increasingly withdrawing from 401(k) accounts as average balances fall, per Fidelity. Consumer stress signals accumulating alongside CEO confidence declining per Axios.

bullets.title: JPM macro calendar: CPI + ORCL earnings June 10, ECB June 11, FOMC June 17
bullets.body: Key macro events next week include US CPI (June 10 alongside ORCL earnings), ECB rate decision June 11 at 8:15am ET, US PPI June 11, and Fed meeting June 17. The G7 Summit runs June 15-17 with a potential Xi-US meeting in 2H 2026. Piper Sandler previews May NFP at +100k.
